w:s01.text: The jab measures and blinds; the cross travels down the same line.

w:s02.text: The double jab steals distance, and the second jab hides the cross.

w:s03.text: Jab high lifts the guard; the cross goes under it to the body.

w:s04.text: Jab to the body drops the hands; the cross goes to the open chin.

w:s05.text: The up jab splits the guard from below; the cross follows through the gap.

w:s06.text: The normal jab makes them shell high; the up jab comes under the gloves.

w:s07.text: Touch with the up jab from range and leave before they can answer.

w:s08.text: Land the one two and leave on an angle. Never stay to admire it.

w:s09.text: The jab feint freezes them; the cross lands while they are still reacting.

w:s10.text: Fake the cross so they cover; jab and cross land as they open back up.

w:s11.text: Finishing on the jab keeps them on the end of your reach while you reset.

w:s12.text: Same cross on two levels: they can only guard one of them.

w:s13.text: The teep after the cross pushes them straight back out to your range.

w:s14.text: The teep stops their step; the jab and cross catch them while they reset.

w:s15.text: The jab lifts their hands and eyes; the teep lands in the open belly.

w:s16.text: A jab feint makes them lift the guard; drive the cross into the body.

w:s17.text: Jab and angle off: they reset facing an empty spot.

w:s18.text: Pumping jabs set a rhythm; the cross breaks it.

w:s19.text: A long cross from outside, then leave on the angle before they answer.

w:s20.text: The body cross pulls their elbows down; the up jab rises straight through.

w:s21.text: Four straights: every hand comes straight back to the face.

w:s22.text: The double jab: the first finds the range, the second scores.

w:s23.text: Body then head with the same hand: the eyes follow the first one down.

w:s24.text: In MMA a level change sells the takedown; the cross lands as they sprawl.

w:s25.text: They move away from the cross into the hook. Then you leave.

w:e01.text: The lead hook pulls their guard wide; the cross goes down the middle, then step out.

w:e02.text: Cross, hook, cross turns them; pivot out so they punch where you were.

w:e03.text: The hook to the liver drops their elbow; the same hook goes up top. Then leave.

w:e04.text: Punish on the inside, then angle off before they can clinch or trade.

w:p01.text: Your jab invites their jab back; pull just out of range and fire the cross over it.

w:p02.text: Let their punch fall short, then hit the space it left open.

w:p03.text: Pull, then cross and hook while they are overextended. Then leave.

w:p04.text: After the miss they are stretched out; jab and cross before they recover.

w:p05.text: A missed punch leaves the body open; drive the cross into it.

w:p06.text: The up jab comes up under their returning hand; the cross follows.

w:p07.text: The cross loads your hips; ride that turn into the lead head kick.

w:p08.text: The feint draws their counter; pull out of it and punish.

w:p09.text: They answer your one two; pull out of it and cross again.

w:p10.text: Counter, then pivot: they turn into nothing.

w:p11.text: Slip outside their jab and your cross is already loaded.

w:p12.text: Slip outside, cross over the top, hook behind it.

w:p13.text: Roll under the hook and come back with your own hook and cross.

w:p14.text: Parry the jab down and the cross is right there.

w:p15.text: If they keep walking after the miss, teep them back to range.

w:p16.text: After the pull your weight is on the back leg, so the lead leg is free to kick.

w:p17.text: Pull, and come back with the lead hook as they reach.

w:p18.text: Stepping back draws them in; the cross meets them on the step.

w:p19.text: Pull from the one two and fire your cross as their second hand comes back.

w:p20.text: Bait, pull, punish, leave. The whole sniper game in one combo.

w:k01.text: The body cross pulls their elbow down; the rear kick goes over it to the head.

w:k02.text: The cross turns your hips; let the lead leg ride that turn up to the head.

w:k03.text: Punches raise their eyes; the low kick lands where they aren't looking.

w:k04.text: The jab blinds them; the rear head kick comes around the side.

w:k05.text: The teep makes them guard the middle; the head kick goes around it.

w:k06.text: After the cross the rear kick is already loaded; land it on the body.

w:k07.text: Fake the kick so they lift the leg; the cross lands while they stand on one foot.

w:k08.text: The up jab splits the guard upward; the head kick comes around it.

w:k09.text: The lead kick to the body brings their elbow down; the cross follows straight.

w:k10.text: Dutch style: punches up top hide the low kick finish.

w:k11.text: The calf kick makes them shift their weight; the cross catches them flat.

w:k12.text: The hook pulls their guard to one side; the rear kick lands on the other.

w:k13.text: Fake the cross so they cover the centre; the lead kick comes around the side.

w:k14.text: The cross turns you; the lead kick lands on the liver side.

w:k15.text: The low kick drops their eyes; the cross follows up top.

w:k16.text: The body jab pulls their hands down; the lead leg goes high.

w:k17.text: Teep to set range, cross to turn them, lead kick to finish on the open side.

w:k18.text: Fake low, go high: their guard follows the fake down.

w:k19.text: Double teep: the first stops them, the second pushes them out of range.

w:r01.text: After the cross they expect a hook; turn and back kick straight up the middle.

w:r02.text: The low kick drops their eyes; the wheel kick comes around high.

w:r03.text: The teep makes them rebound forward, straight into the knee.

w:r04.text: They brace for the cross; the back kick goes into the belly.

w:r05.text: The jab freezes their guard high; the flying knee comes from underneath.

w:r06.text: If the head kick misses, keep spinning: the wheel kick uses the same turn.

w:t01.text: Three body crosses teach them to drop the elbow; the fourth goes high.

w:t02.text: After repeated one twos they cover high and centre; the lead kick goes around.

w:t03.text: Three identical jabs set the rhythm; the feint breaks it and the cross lands on the flinch.

w:t04.text: Straight jabs make them cover high; the up jab comes underneath on the third.

w:t05.text: Two teeps make them reach for the leg; fake the third and cross over the lowered hand.

w:t06.text: Twice to the body drops their guard; the same entry goes to the head the third time.

w:t07.text: Low kicks pull their eyes and guard down; the same leg comes up high.

w:t08.text: Jab and step back teaches them to chase; the third time, pull and catch them chasing.

w:t09.text: Leaving after the one two invites them to follow; the third time you stay and counter.

w:t10.text: Body kicks make them drop the arm; the same kick goes upstairs. Jones did it to Cormier.

w:t11.text: Two one twos make them shell high; the third cross goes under, to the body.

w:t12.text: Up jabs make them squeeze the guard tight in the middle; the head kick goes around it.

w:t13.text: Teeps make them guard the middle; after the jab, the kick goes high instead.

w:t14.text: Twice they eat the pull counter and cover for the cross; the third answer is the kick.

w:t15.text: They learn to check after the one two; now the kick goes high.

w:t16.text: Feints with no follow-up teach them to ignore it; the next one is real.

w:t17.text: Calf kicks make them lift the leg early; fake it and cross while they stand on one foot.

w:t18.text: Each combo adds a strike; they defend the last pattern, not the new one.

w:t19.text: Two empty pulls make them commit to the counter; the third time it's waiting for them.

w:t20.text: Cross feints make them cover their face; the real cross goes to the body.

w:d01.text: Catch the jab with the rear hand and fire the cross back down the line.

w:d02.text: Lean back just enough for the jab to fall short, then cross over it.

w:d03.text: Slip outside the jab; your cross is loaded on that side.

w:d04.text: Step out of range, then come back as they recover.

w:d05.text: After the pull your weight is back and the lead leg is free.

w:d06.text: The cross falls short when you pull; your cross comes back while their chin is open.

w:d07.text: Slip outside the cross and the lead hook is loaded on that side.

w:d08.text: Take it on the shoulder and fire the cross straight back.

w:d09.text: Pull, and hook them as their cross comes back.

w:d10.text: Parry the cross across with the lead hand, then answer straight down the middle.

w:d11.text: Roll under the hook and come back with your own hook and cross.

w:d12.text: The hook passes in front of your face; the cross goes through the middle it opened.

w:d13.text: Glove to the temple, answer straight, and leave before the next one.

w:d14.text: Block the rear hook; your lead hook is the shortest answer.

w:d15.text: The overhand is long and slow: step back, let it miss, punish the gap.

w:d16.text: Parry the jab, pull from the cross, and cross back over it.

w:d17.text: Step back from both, then cross as they finish.

w:d18.text: Parry both jabs and the cross is free on the third beat.

w:d19.text: Check with the lead shin and cross while they land square.

w:d20.text: Pull the leg back so the kick misses, then cross as they swing through.

w:d21.text: Check, then answer kick for kick.

w:d22.text: Turn the knee out to check the calf, then cross as they land.

w:d23.text: Check and teep straight away so they can't follow up.

w:d24.text: Catch the body kick and cross while they hop on one leg.

w:d25.text: Block it, then kick back on the same side while they reset.

w:d26.text: Block high, arm tight to the head, then cross while they land.

w:d27.text: Lean back and let it pass in front of you, then punish as they turn open.

w:d28.text: Block with the rear arm, then jab and cross before they reset their feet.

w:d29.text: Step back out of the arc; their hip is open as the kick passes.

w:d30.text: Parry the teep across your body; they turn sideways and the cross is open.

w:d31.text: Catch the teep and cross while they balance on one leg.

w:d32.text: Step off the line and low kick the leg they are standing on.

i:counter-hard.text: Pull counters and defence. Hard day.

i:counter-tech.text: Pull counters and defence. Technical day.

f:warm.text: Warm-up round. Loose and light. Jab, cross, move your feet.

f:burnout.text: Final round. Burnout. Straight punches, nonstop, as fast as you can.

f:techfinal.text: Final round. Slow and technical. Perfect form, exhale on every strike.

f:snipe1.text: Round one. The jab. Double it, up jab it, and leave.

f:snipe2.text: Round two. Straights on two levels. Head and body.

f:snipe3.text: Round three. Traps. Repeat the pattern, then break it.

f:snipe4.text: Round four. Snipe and exit. Every combo ends with you out of range.

f:kicks1.text: Round one. Punches into kicks. The hands hide the legs.

f:kicks2.text: Round two. Head kicks. Set them up, never throw them naked.

f:kicks3.text: Round three. Kick traps. Condition low and middle, then go high.

f:kicks4.text: Round four. Teep and range. Keep them on the end of your leg.

f:counter1.text: Round one. Pull counters. Bait, pull, punish.

f:counter2.text: Round two. Defence against punches. Defend first, then answer.

f:counter3.text: Round three. Defence against kicks. Check, block, catch, then answer.

f:counter4.text: Round four. Everything. Bait, defend, counter, exit.

p:done.text: Session done. Good work. Rate it and log it.
